cards.explanation: The answer is that very much of the land remains to be possessed. The LORD says, "You are old and well along in years, but very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Joshua, Israel's leader, has done a LOT, and there's still a lot left. I know that feeling, friends. You finish one tray and the counter is still covered.

The answer is the LORD Himself. He says, "…I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) That covers all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. He puts Himself right in that sentence as the One who drives them out. Then He gives Joshua a different job: divide the land by lot.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you." (Joshua 13:6) Even with land still to be taken, He wants it divided. That tells me He's serious about what He promised, friends.

The answer is nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh. The LORD says, "Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) So this land is for nine tribes plus half of Manasseh. The other half of Manasseh had already received its inheritance from Moses beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). Keep an eye on that half, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day." (Joshua 13:13) Just before that, Moses, Israel's leader, had struck down Og's kingdom and dispossessed them (Joshua 13:12). Then this verse turns and says these two peoples were not driven out. I think that's a detail worth holding onto, bakers.

The answer is the food offerings to the LORD. Levi is the tribe set apart to carry the ark and serve the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:8), and Moses gave them no land. Their inheritance is this: "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) A few verses later it's said again: "The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:33) Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh got territory from Moses, and Levi got a promise instead. I think that's worth a second look, friends.
